scenarios.note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up of right heel ulcer.

HPI
Pt is an 80-year-old female presenting for f/u of a non-pressure chronic ulcer of the right heel. Pt reports the wound has not improved with current conservative management. Describes increasing pain and drainage over the last 2 weeks. Denies systemic symptoms like fever or chills. No recent trauma to the site. Pt is seeking evaluation for surgical intervention.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10mg QD
Atorvastatin 20mg QD
Aspirin 81mg QD

Review of Systems
Constitutional: Denies fever, chills, fatigue.
Integumentary: Positive for chronic ulcer on right heel. No other skin changes.
Musculoskeletal: Positive for localized pain at right heel.
Neuro: Denies numbness or tingling.
All other systems reviewed and negative.

Social History
Retired. Lives at home with her daughter. Non-smoker. No alcohol use.

Family History
Mother: Hypertension, Stroke.
Father: Heart disease.

Vitals
BP: 132/84
HR: 76 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on RA
Ht/Wt: 5'4", 145 lbs

Recent Labs
WBC: 8.2 (WNL)
HbA1c: 6.4%
eGFR: 68
CRP: 15.2 (Elevated)

Exam
General: Pt alert, oriented x3, in no acute distress.
Skin: Non-pressure chronic ulcer of the right heel noted. Wound measures 3x2 cm. Significant necrosis of bone is visible at the base of the wound. Purulent drainage noted. Surrounding tissue is erythematous. No fluctuance or warmth noted.
Musculoskeletal: Decreased ROM of right ankle due to pain.
Neuro: Sensation intact to light touch.

Assessment
1. Non-pressure chronic ulcer of the right heel with necrosis of bone.

Plan
1. Surgical debridement of right heel planned for next week.
2. Wound care: Continue daily dressing changes with saline and gauze.
3. F/u with surgical team for debridement.
4. Pt to monitor for increased redness or drainage before surgery.
